lead.why: Abstract: 'The most potent compound with IC50 = 0.6 nM was the 3',4'-dichloro-BPH 16'.

reactions.conditions: Method A: phthalic anhydride (2.2 mmol), the phenylacetic acid derivative (2.7 mmol), potassium acetate (0.26 mmol), toluene (5 mL), Dean-Stark, N2, 220-240 C, 4 h (for 16); yield 58 %. Z isomer.
reactions.source: Section 2.1 and Section 4.1.2 (Method A; compound 16 entry), main article; Scheme 1

notes: Neither starting material is named in the experimental text; both are generic: the general procedure says 'phthalic anhydride and the corresponding 2-phenylacetic acid derivative' and 'All commercial chemicals ... used as purchased'. The 3,4-dichlorophenylacetic acid is inferred from the product name (no doubt). The Z configuration is stated in the paper (NOE/ROESY). Co-products are CO2 and H2O. No SI file in the bundle (not needed).
